answer: Sybil resistance starts by making each identity expensive to fake. An agent posts a bond that is slashed the moment its content hash matches another account's submission, so a zephyr of cloned answers burns real capital instead of costing nothing. Peers then exchange signed attestations, and a project's fable only counts as signal when independent stakers back it, each one losing their bond for vouching on duplicates. A thousand fake identities now cost a thousand bonds.
